questions.question: How do neural networks compute gradients of the loss with respect to each weight layer by layer?
questions.reply: Neural networks compute gradients of the loss with respect to each weight layer by layer using backpropagation. This method avoids inefficiency by computing the gradient of each layer from back to front, specifically the gradient of the weighted input of each layer, denoted by . The gradients of the weights of previous layers are then computed recursively. This process involves matrix multiplications and the use of auxiliary quantities, such as the "error at level ", which is the gradient of the input values at that level. The gradient of the weights in a layer is computed using these quantities and matrix multiplications. [1][2][3][4]
